attributions.rationale: The sequence `dissolve Parliament`, `ending its current term`, and `call an election` presents Parliament as the particular elected legislature whose bounded term ends at dissolution, so sense:002 is the natural attribution. Sense:001 can denote the continuing institution, but that institutional reading does not itself supply the explicitly terminated current term attached to the headword here.

In `member of parliament`, parliament is the institution or representative body of which she becomes a member, selecting sense:001. Sense:002 denotes a particular parliamentary term or post-election parliament and cannot by itself express the institutional membership relation encoded by `member of parliament`.

discriminating_terms: general election produced a hung parliament
attributions.rationale: The wording `general election produced a hung parliament` identifies a particular legislature constituted by that election, and `for the new term` explicitly bounds it as the new parliamentary term, selecting sense:002. Sense:001 describes Parliament as an enduring institution or collective actor, but does not capture this election-created, term-specific instance of the headword.

In `Parliament passed the bill`, the headword is the institutional legislative body acting as agent of passage, which directly selects sense:001. Sense:002 is a bounded parliament or its duration; the temporal unit itself is not what performs the legislative act in this unqualified institutional-agent construction.

The prepositional frame `during the current parliament` makes parliament the bounded time span within which passage may occur, selecting sense:002. Sense:001 is an institution or collective participant, not the duration supplied as the complement of `during` here.

The phrase `during this parliament` uses the headword as a delimited period in which the measure will be introduced, so sense:002 is uniquely natural. Sense:001 denotes the institutional body and does not furnish the temporal interval required by `during this parliament`.

In `in the next parliament`, next orders parliament as the subsequent post-election legislative term in which reconsideration should happen, selecting sense:002. Sense:001 is the standing institution and is not naturally one member of a sequential series marked by `the next parliament` in this temporal frame.

The complement `before Parliament` presents Parliament as the institutional deliberative body before which a bill is formally pending, selecting sense:001. Sense:002 denotes a particular parliament or its duration, but that time-bounded sense does not supply the institutional forum relation expressed by `before Parliament`.

The construction `elected to Parliament` makes Parliament the representative institution to which he gains membership, so sense:001 is the natural attribution. Sense:002 refers to a particular parliamentary term or instance, but it does not independently express the destination-of-membership relation carried by `to Parliament`.

In the fixed legislative expression `Act of Parliament`, Parliament denotes the institution whose enactment gives the Act its authority, selecting sense:001. Sense:002 denotes a bounded parliament or its lifespan and does not express the institutional source relation in `Act of Parliament`.

The duration expression `the lifetime of a parliament` treats a parliament as a bounded post-election existence over which reform may be completed, selecting sense:002. Sense:001 is the continuing institution or collective actor and does not naturally have the finite institutional term measured by `lifetime` here.
